gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Galaxy Tab Active5 Pro takes two 5,050 mAh batteries (10,100 mAh combined) and can swap one at a time while staying powered (Samsung's 'Dual Hot-Swap'), while the Panasonic TOUGHBOOK G2 only hot-swaps if the optional bridge battery is fitted, so 'replaceable battery' in ChatGPT's checklist does not mean the tablet stays on during a swap.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Panasonic NA G2 page (connect.na.panasonic.com), read 2026-11-14. It says only 'Optional bridge battery enables hot-swap battery replacement', so it covers half the G2 story and nothing about the other tablets. ChatGPT's answer flattened this into 'hot-swappable battery support' for the G2 and 'Replaceable battery or full-shift runtime' in its table. It never says hot-swap is an add-on on the G2, never mentions Samsung's Dual Hot-Swap or No Battery Mode, and says nothing about battery swapping on the Dell. No Samsung page appears among ChatGPT's 18 results. The rottenwifi.com roundup (result 11) returned HTTP 502 and could not be checked.
decides: For shifts longer than one charge, the Tab Active5 Pro, about $776 at Newegg per ChatGPT's card, keeps running through a battery change with no extra hardware: two batteries come in the box and you swap one at a time. That makes it the low-cost pick that also keeps working through a swap. The G2 (about $3,802 per ChatGPT's card) does this only if the bridge-battery option is ordered, so a buyer has to check the configuration. The Dell Pro Rugged 12 has dual hot-swappable batteries as standard. Samsung's No Battery Mode suits a vehicle or kiosk mount but slows the CPU/GPU and lowers screen brightness, so it is not a fix for outdoor use.
